gaps.message: Printed part 9(b)(iii): "The isotope of neptunium produced by americium-241 is also radioactive. ... The half-life of neptunium is longer than two million years. Using this information, explain the advantage of this long half-life for the use and safe disposal of a household smoke alarm." The official mark scheme credits "low(er) (initial) activity OR few emissions per unit time" (M1) "so smoke detectors are not hazardous to humans OR so disposal of old detectors is cheap / easy" (A1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 5.2.4 Half-life Supplement item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including (a) household fire (smoke) alarms" (printed page 36 PDF / page 34 footer, Supplement column). The pinned taxonomy owns only two details under official code 5.2.4: half-life.tables-and-curves (pinned applicability core, printed Core item 1 - the definition and simple half-life calculations from tables or decay curves) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (pinned applicability supplement, printed Supplement item 2 - calculating half-life where background has not been subtracted). Neither is source-equivalent to justifying a radionuclide for an application by its half-life: the pinned Supplement detail names the background-subtraction operation, not the applications bullet, so no same-tier detail carries the assessed statement. This is an owning-detail gap in the pinned taxonomy (the applications bullet has no detail), not a content gap, and no nearest label was forced. Recorded identically to the settled practice of batch-114 (0625-2024-w-23-q37) and batch-117 (0625-2024-w-42-q10) for the same 5.2.4 item 3 bullet.

gaps.message: Printed part: (c). The marked operation is that the gravitational field strength at the surface of a planet depends on the mass of the planet (the weight/g of a mass on Venus is smaller than on the Earth because Venus has the smaller mass; the official mark scheme credits 'value smaller than 9.8 (N / kg)' B1 and 'Venus has smaller mass ORA OR gravitational field strength depends on / proportional to mass' B1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 6.1.2 item 3(a) 'Know that the strength of the gravitational field at the surface of a planet depends on the mass of the planet', which the printed syllabus places in the Core column of PDF page 39 (x0 = 79.4). The pinned overlay exposes no source-equivalent Core detail: space-solar-system.orbits-and-gravity and mass-weight.gravitational-field are both stored with applicability ["supplement"], while the only Core detail under official code 6.1.2 (space-solar-system.objects-and-formation) owns the Solar System inventory and accretion-formation Core statements, not the field-strength/mass relationship. Because the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/32 the validator refuses either Supplement-applicability detail, so the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped. Applicability check performed by x-coordinate on the pinned official syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c).

gaps.message: Printed part: (b). The marked operation is the mechanical working equation, work done = force x distance (the 14 N force pushes the device 4.5 m; the official mark scheme credits '63 (J)' A3, '(work done =) 14 x 4.5' C2 and '(work done =) force x distance (moved in direction of force)' C1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 1.7.2 item 2 'Recall and use the equation for mechanical working W = Fd = delta-E'. Its owning detail in the pinned overlay is work.mechanical-equation with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 1.7.2), and because the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/32 the validator refuses that detail (a Core paper cannot select a Supplement detail). Applicability defect checked against the pinned official syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 17 / printed page 15, section 1.7.2) where item 2 'Recall and use the equation for mechanical working W = Fd = delta-E' is printed in the Core column and the 1.7.2 Supplement column carries no items at all. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: work.energy-transfer owns printed Core 1.7.2 item 1 'Understand that mechanical or electrical work done is equal to the energy transferred' but does not state the force x distance equation the marking credits, so the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped. Diagram 2 shows how a smoke particle moves randomly. microscope air particles and smoke particles light diagram 1 diagram 2 random movement eye Why do the smoke particles move randomly? A They are hit by air particles. B They are less dense than air. C They are moved by convection currents. D They gain energy from the light.

gaps.message: The paired QP/MS assess the random (Brownian) movement of smoke particles as caused by collisions with air particles: QP 10 (0625/11 M/J 24) asks "Why do the smoke particles move randomly?" and the printed mark scheme keys answer A "They are hit by air particles". The pinned 2023_2025 taxonomy owns that collision content only in particle-model.forces-and-collisions, whose on-disk detail_applicability is ["supplement"] (official code 2.1.2); this is a core paper (on-disk paper_tier "core", component 11) and calibration_final._validate_selection rejects a Supplement detail on a Core paper ("Core paper cannot select Supplement detail"). No core-applicable detail expresses the collision cause, so the nearest core detail particle-model.arrangement-motion is retained only as a non-mastery placeholder.

questions.accessibleText: 26 There is a current I in a resistor of resistance R. The potential difference (p.d.) across the resistor is V. Which equation gives the power P dissipated by the resistor? A P = IR B P = IV C P = R I D P = V I

gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (Q26 stem 'There is a current I in a resistor of resistance R. The potential difference (p.d.) across the resistor is V.' and options A-D). The marked operation is identifying the equation giving the power P dissipated by the resistor, P = IV (the printed keyed answer is B). The printed owning bullet is the 2023-2025 Core bullet 4.2.5 item 2 'Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV', whose owning detail electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations is stored with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 4.2.5), so the Core paper 0625/12 cannot select it. Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 29 / printed page 27, section 4.2.5) where item 2 'Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV' and item 3 'Recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt' are printed in the Core column and the 4.2.5 Supplement column carries no items at all. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: electrical-work-power.energy-transfer owns printed Core 4.2.5 item 1 'Understand that electric circuits transfer energy from a source of electrical energy, such as an electrical cell or mains supply, to the circuit components and then into the surroundings' and does not state the P = IV equation, so it is carried only as the sibling Core owner under official code 4.2.5 and the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped.

A the charge flowing through the resistor B the energy transferred by the resistor C the power dissipated by the resistor D the resistance of the resistor

gaps.message: Paired QP/MS inspection of 0625/13 Q27 shows the printed item gives a current I in a resistor for a time t with potential difference V and asks what the product IVt represents, and the official mark scheme awards row Q27 answer B – 1 mark, the energy transferred by the resistor. That assessed operation is the electrical energy equation E = IVt, which the frozen 2023_2025 taxonomy exposes only as the Supplement-only detail electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations, and a Core paper cannot select a Supplement detail; official code 4.2.5 exposes only electrical-work-power.energy-transfer as Core (understand that electric circuits transfer energy from a source to the circuit components and then into the surroundings), which is not equivalent to the E = IVt operation. The pinned official 2023-2025 guide (source official-2023-2025, sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, page 29) prints 'recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt' in the Core column of 4.2.5 (word x0 = 79.37), so this is recorded as an unresolved applicability conflict rather than forcing Q27 into the nearby Core label. The retained Core 4.2.5 anchor is not semantic approval of the E = IVt operation.

gaps.message: Printed part: (c). The marked operation is the electrical power equation (the power transferred in the lamp at 12 V and 0.41 A; the official mark scheme credits '4.9' A3, '0.41 x 12 OR 0.41^2 x 29' (C2), '(P =) I x V in any form OR (P =) I^2 x R' (C1) and 'W' B1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 4.2.5 item 2 'Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV'. Its owning detail in the pinned overlay is electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations (era 2023_2025, official code 4.2.5), stored with applicability ["supplement"], and because the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/33 the validator refuses that detail (a Core paper cannot select a Supplement detail). Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 29), whose 4.2.5 Supplement column is empty and lists P = IV as Core; the Core owner electrical-work-power.energy-transfer does not cover the power-equation bullet, so no Core detail is source-equivalent and the part is not legally labelable on the pinned taxonomy. Marked unresolved rather than forcing a nearest Core label.

gaps.message: Printed parts credit spring/load-extension content. 0625-2024-s-61-q1: MS 1(b) 'extension e = 21.6 when L = 5.00 N'; 1(c) the L-e graph; 1(d) the gradient triangle; 1(e) 'k = G and to 2 or 3 significant figures' with unit N / cm. 0625-2024-s-62-q1: MS 1(c) k1 (expect 25.0); 1(e)(iii) k2 = 23.5 to 26.4; 1(f) a statement comparing k1 and k2. gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (Q22 stem and options A-D). The marked criterion (early-Universe gamma radiation that has shifted into the microwave region, with wavelength increased and speed unchanged) is the printed Supplement-only bullet 6.2.3(6) 'Explain that the CMBR was produced shortly after the Universe was formed and that this radiation has been expanded into the microwave region of the electromagnetic spectrum as the Universe expanded', owned by the Supplement-only detail space-universe.cmb-hubble-and-age. The printed Core bullets of 6.2.3 are 1 (Milky Way is one of many billions of galaxies, diameter approx. 100 000 light-years), 2 (redshift as an increase in the observed wavelength of radiation emitted from receding stars and galaxies), 3 (light from distant galaxies appears redshifted compared with light emitted on the Earth) and 4 (redshift in light from distant galaxies is evidence that the Universe is expanding and supports the Big Bang Theory): none of them covers primordial radiation filling the Universe being stretched by expansion, so no Core detail is source-equivalent and space-universe.milky-way-redshift-big-bang is recorded only as the Core owner of subtopic space-universe for official code 6.2.3, not as a source-equivalent label.

gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (Q37 stem, graph and options A-D). The item assesses the printed 2023-2025 Supplement bullet 5.2.4(3)(d) 'Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including ... (d) measuring and controlling thicknesses of materials with the choice of radiations used linked to penetration and absorption' - a beta-particle source and detector whose count rate falls as the paper thickness increases, with the rollers squeezing below 12 counts/s and stopping above 13 counts/s. The pinned taxonomy owns only one Supplement detail under mapping 5.2.4, half-life.background-not-subtracted (= Supplement bullet 5.2.4(2), calculating half-life from data where background has not been subtracted), and no detail at all for the isotope-application bullet 5.2.4(3)(d). The printed Core bullets of 5.2.4 are only bullet 1 (define half-life as the time taken for half the nuclei in any sample to decay and use it in simple calculations from tables or decay curves), which does not cover choosing a radionuclide for a thickness gauge; half-life.tables-and-curves is recorded only as the Core owner of subtopic half-life for official code 5.2.4, not as a source-equivalent label. The candidate nearest labels are not source-equivalent either: nuclear-emissions.nature-ionisation-penetration (Core, 5.2.2) owns the relative ionising and penetrating abilities of alpha, beta and gamma emissions, not an absorption-based thickness-control application, and nuclear-emissions.fields-and-applications (Supplement, 5.2.2) owns deflection of the emissions in electric/magnetic fields and the explanation of their relative ionising effects, not isotope selection for measuring and controlling material thickness. No Core or Supplement detail in the pinned overlay owns the assessed thickness-control application, so the row stays unresolved rather than forcing a label.
gaps.proposedMaterialConcept: half-life (needs a Supplement-band companion detail under 5.2.4 for the isotope-application bullet 5.2.4(3)(d), measuring and controlling thicknesses of materials linked to penetration and absorption)

gaps.message: Printed Q4(b) states that a 15 W lamp is switched on for 5.0 minutes and requires the electrical work done in the lamp circuit, credited by the official mark scheme through the power-energy relation ((energy =) 4500 (J); (energy =) 15 x 300; 'power = energy ÷ time OR (energy =) power x time'; '5.0 minutes = 300 s'). The only project detail naming that equation is power.equation, whose pinned applicability is Supplement-only, and Core paper 31 cannot select it. The Core detail of the same official code, power.rate-of-transfer, names power as work done / energy transferred per unit time but does not carry the equation the mark scheme credits, and neither work.energy-transfer (1.7.2) nor electrical-work-power.energy-transfer (4.2.5) is source-equivalent because both state the work/energy equivalence only. The pinned official 2023-2025 guide (source official-2023-2025, sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 18) prints 'Define power as work done per unit time and also as energy transferred per unit time; recall and use the equations (a) P = W/t (b) P = ∆E/t' in the Core column of 1.7.4 with an empty Supplement column, so this is a pinned applicability conflict, not a content gap. No Core label is forced.

gaps.message: Printed part 10(c): "Suggest a use of a radioactive isotope with a half-life of one hour. Explain why a short half-life is suitable for this use." The official mark scheme credits "medical tracers OR medical imaging OR medical diagnosis" - B1 and "any one from: keep dose low / does not stay in body too long / less damage (to body)" - B1, i.e. the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 5.2.4 Half-life Supplement item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including ... (e) diagnosis and treatment of cancer using gamma rays" (printed page 36 PDF / page 34 footer, Supplement column, x0 = 309.0). The pinned taxonomy owns only two details under official code 5.2.4: half-life.tables-and-curves (pinned applicability core, printed Core item 1 only - the definition and simple half-life calculations from tables or decay curves) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (pinned applicability supplement, printed Supplement item 2 only - calculating half-life where background has not been subtracted). Neither is source-equivalent to choosing or justifying a radionuclide for an application by its half-life: the pinned Supplement detail names the background-subtraction operation, not the applications bullet, so no same-tier detail carries the assessed statement. This is an owning-detail gap in the pinned taxonomy (the applications bullet has no detail), not a content gap, and no nearest label was forced.

gaps.message: Printed part (b)(ii) 'Calculate the energy transferred electrically when the current calculated in (b)(i) is present in resistor Q for 5 minutes' is credited by MS 6(b)(ii) '610 J  OR  620 J' A3 with 'E = I × V × t  OR  (E =) V × I × t  OR  (E =) 12 × 0.17 × 300' C1 and '300 (s) OR 5 × 60' C1, i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 4.2.5 item 3 'Recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt' (syllabus PDF p.29, printed page 27, Core column x=62.4, next to Core item 2 'P = IV'). The owning pinned detail electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations carries applicability ['supplement'] only, so the Core-printed statement has no same-tier owning detail: labelling it 'supplement' would misstate the printed column and no source-equivalent Core detail exists. The only Core-applicability detail under 4.2.5 is electrical-work-power.energy-transfer, whose printed bullet is item 1 'Understand that electric circuits transfer energy from a source of electrical energy, such as an electrical cell or mains supply, to the circuit components and then into the surroundings', not the electrical energy equation. The nearest equation detail elsewhere is 1.7.2 work.mechanical-equation, which owns the mechanical equation W = Fd = ΔE (and is itself printed Core but pinned Supplement), so it is not source-equivalent for E = IVt. The row therefore stays unresolved for this part rather than forcing a nearest label onto a Core-printed statement.

gaps.message: Printed part (c) is credited by MS 3(c) 'a and b lengths measured correctly' (technique) and 'n in range 1.30 to 1.70 from correct calculation' for a value n calculated from the printed n = a / b. The only detail owning refractive index is refraction.refractive-index-and-fibres under official code 3.2.2 (Refraction of light), whose pinned applicability is ['supplement'] and whose printed 2023-2025 syllabus statements sit in the SUPPLEMENT column only: item 6 'Define refractive index, n, as the ratio of the speeds of a wave in two different regions' and item 7 'Recall and use the equation n = sin i / sin r' (syllabus SHA256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF p.24 / printed p.22, both at x0=326.0; the Core header prints at x0=62.4 and the Supplement header at x0=309.0). This is a P5 all_candidates paper and taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects a Supplement content selection on an all_candidates paper ('all_candidates content selection must use Core or practical skills'), so the owning detail cannot be selected at this tier. No same-tier detail is source-equivalent: the Core detail refraction.experiment-and-total-internal-reflection rests only on the printed Core items 1-5 of 3.2.2 ('Define and use the terms normal, angle of incidence and angle of refraction'; 'Describe an experiment to show refraction of light by transparent blocks of different shapes'; 'Describe the passage of light through a transparent material'; 'State the meaning of critical angle'; 'Describe internal reflection and total internal reflection'), none of which prints the refractive index, its definition or any equation for n. No nearest Core label was forced; part (c) is left unresolved and unlabelled for a taxonomy-owner decision.

gaps.message: Printed part: (b). The marked operation is the mechanical working equation, work done = force x distance (the 8.0 N weight of the load is lifted a vertical distance of 0.60 m; the official mark scheme credits '4.8 (J)' A3, '(work done =) 8(.0) x 0.6' C2 and '(work done =) force x distance (moved in direction of force)' C1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 1.7.2 item 2 'Recall and use the equation for mechanical working W = Fd = delta-E'. Its owning detail in the pinned overlay is work.mechanical-equation, stored with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 1.7.2), and because the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/32 the validator refuses that detail (a Core paper cannot select a Supplement detail). Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 17 / printed page 15, section 1.7.2) where item 2 is printed in the Core column (word x0 = 79.4) and the 1.7.2 Supplement column carries no items at all. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: work.energy-transfer owns printed Core 1.7.2 item 1 'Understand that mechanical or electrical work done is equal to the energy transferred' but does not state the force x distance equation the marking credits, so it is carried only as the sibling Core owner under official code 1.7.2 and the marked operation is left unlabelled rather than force-mapped. This is the work.mechanical-equation printed_core_contradicts_pinned_supplement case recorded in data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-applicability-ledger.json.

gaps.message: Printed part: (c). The marked operation is the electrical power equation P = IV (the 0.40 A current in the motor at a potential difference of 6.0 V; the official mark scheme credits '2.4 (W)' A3, '(power input =) 0.4(0) x 6(.0)' C2 and '(power input =) I x V' C1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 Core bullet 4.2.5 item 2 'Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV'. Its owning detail in the pinned overlay is electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations, stored with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 4.2.5), and because the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/32 the validator refuses that detail (a Core paper cannot select a Supplement detail). Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 29 / printed page 27, section 4.2.5) where items 2 'Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV' and 3 'Recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt' are printed in the Core column (word x0 = 79.4) and the 4.2.5 Supplement column carries no items at all. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: electrical-work-power.energy-transfer owns printed Core 4.2.5 item 1 'Understand that electric circuits transfer energy from a source of electrical energy ... to the circuit components and then into the surroundings' but does not state the P = IV equation the marking credits, and power.rate-of-transfer (printed Core 1.7.4 item 1) states power as work done or energy transferred per unit time, not I x V, so neither is forced onto the marked operation. gaps.message: Printed part 9(b)(i): "Strontium-90 is used to measure the thickness of metal sheets in industry. ... Suggest why strontium-90 is a suitable radioactive source to measure the thickness of the metal sheets." The official mark scheme credits "(there is a) different count rate with different thicknesses of metal OR number of beta-particles detected varies with thickness" A2 with "(beta (beta) particles) can penetrate thin / 0.75 mm metal OR (beta (beta) particles) are stopped by thick metal" C1, i.e. the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 5.2.4 Half-life Supplement item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including ... (d) measuring and controlling thicknesses of materials with the choice of radiations used linked to penetration and absorption" (PDF page 36 / printed page 34 footer, Supplement column, x0 = 326.0; the Core header prints at x0 = 62.4 and the Supplement header at x0 = 309.0). The pinned taxonomy owns only two details under official code 5.2.4: half-life.tables-and-curves (on-disk detail_applicability ["core"], printed Core item 1 only - the half-life definition and simple calculations from tables or decay curves) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (on-disk detail_applicability ["supplement"], printed Supplement item 2 only - calculating half-life where background has not been subtracted). Neither is source-equivalent to choosing or justifying a radionuclide for a thickness-measuring application: the printed Supplement applications bullet 3(d) has no owning detail, so no detail on any tier carries the assessed statement. This is an owning-detail gap in the pinned taxonomy, not a content gap, and no nearest label was forced. Same settled disposition as batch-114 (0625-2024-w-23-q37), batch-117 (0625-2024-w-42-q10) and batch-131 (0625-2025-s-22-q35) for the same 5.2.4 item 3 bullet.
gaps.proposedMaterialConcept: no owning detail for the printed 5.2.4 item 3 applications bullet (thickness measurement)

After the decay-curve percentage reading (B1, labelled here on printed Core 5.2.4 item 1), the official mark scheme credits "Any one from: count rate / activity (too) low (to detect differences in thickness) owtte; detector needs high activity (to detect differences in thickness) owtte; count rate / activity too close to background owtte; less difference in activity for different thicknesses owtte" B1, i.e. the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 5.2.4 Half-life Supplement item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including ... (d) measuring and controlling thicknesses of materials with the choice of radiations used linked to penetration and absorption" (PDF page 36 / printed page 34 footer, Supplement column, x0 = 326.0; the Core header prints at x0 = 62.4 and the Supplement header at x0 = 309.0). Under official code 5.2.4 the pinned taxonomy owns only half-life.tables-and-curves (on-disk detail_applicability ["core"], printed Core item 1) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (on-disk detail_applicability ["supplement"], printed Supplement item 2); neither states the half-life-applications bullet, so the credited suitability statement for replacing the source has no owning detail on any tier and the printed part is only partially labelable. The decay-curve reading that precedes it is labelled half-life.tables-and-curves in this row's subparts; no nearest label was forced for the un-owned suitability statement.

Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ['supplement'] versus the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (SHA256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, PDF page 17 / printed page 15, section 1.7.2, Core-column body line_x0 = 62.4) where item 2 is printed in the Core column and the 1.7.2 Supplement column carries no items at all; data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-syllabus-column-evidence.json records printed_column 'core' with verdict_vs_pinned printed_core_contradicts_pinned_supplement for work.mechanical-equation and data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-applicability-ledger.json records the confirmed contradicting print. gaps.message: Printed part (c)(ii) asks the candidate to 'Explain why a source with a short half-life must be used' for the technetium isotope injected into the body to detect cancer in an organ (half-life 6 hours, gamma emitter, radiation detected outside the body). The official mark scheme credits 'after a few days / some time, little radiation is emitted owtte' - B1. That is the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 5.2.4 Half-life Supplement column item 3: 'Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including: ... (e) diagnosis and treatment of cancer using gamma rays' (syllabus PDF page 36, Supplement column, body word x0 = 326.0). The pinned overlay's 5.2.4 mapping owns only two details: half-life.tables-and-curves (pinned applicability [core] - the printed Core item 1 definition and simple calculations from tables or decay curves) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (pinned applicability [supplement] - the printed Supplement item 2 calculation where background radiation has not been subtracted). Neither detail states the choice-of-isotope-by-half-life-and-emission application bullet, so no owned detail legally expresses this assessed operation on any tier, and no nearest label is forced. Settled precedent for this exact operation: batch-104 0625-2024-s-43-q10 (c)(i)/(c)(ii), batch-117 0625-2024-w-42-q10 (c) and batch-114 q37, all written unresolved with the same gap.
gaps.printed_bullet: Supplement statement 5.2.4 item 3: 'Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including: (a) household fire (smoke) alarms (b) irradiating food to kill bacteria (c) sterilisation of equipment using gamma rays (d) measuring and controlling thicknesses of materials with the choice of radiations used linked to penetration and absorption (e) diagnosis and treatment of cancer using gamma rays' (syllabus PDF page 36, printed page 34, Supplement column, word x0 = 326.0).

gaps.message: Printed part (d)(i) of 0625-2025-s-53-q3 materially assesses COMBINED RESISTANCE and has no tier-legal owner on this Core (all_candidates P5) paper. The question gives two equal resistors: circuit A (R1 in parallel with R2) is worked up with RA = 2R, circuit B (R1 alone) with RB = R from circuit B, and circuit C (R1 in series with R2) with RC = R / 2; MS 3(d)(i) credits 'calculations correct' and 'RA RB and RC within 10% of each other', i.e. the equal-resistor case of the series and parallel combined-resistance relations. The printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c) places those statements in the CORE column of 4.3.2 Series and parallel circuits on syllabus PDF page 30 (printed page 28): Core item 4 (x0 = 79.4) 'Calculate the combined resistance of two or more resistors in series' and Core item 6 (x0 = 79.4) 'State that the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel is less than that of either resistor by itself', while the Supplement column (x0 = 309.0 / 326.0) prints item 10 'Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel'. On disk the era 2023_2025 code 4.3.2 owns exactly two details: series-parallel.rules-and-lamps with detail_applicability ['core'] and series-parallel.combined-values with detail_applicability ['supplement']; only series-parallel.combined-values owns the combined-resistance statements, and it is pinned supplement, so the printed-Core part has no same-tier owner and the Core sibling series-parallel.rules-and-lamps does not state the combined-resistance relations (it is not source-equivalent). This is an all_candidates P5/P6 paper and taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects a Supplement content selection on such a paper ('all_candidates content selection must use Core or practical skills'), so the part is not labelable and no Core-adjacent detail was substituted. The remaining printed parts are carried by the code-free practical primary, the practical_skills entries and the Core 4.2.4 / 4.2.2 secondaries.
gaps.proposedMaterialConcept: an era-scoped taxonomy re-seal that gives the printed 2023-2025 Core 4.3.2 combined-resistance statements (items 4 and 6) a Core-applicability owner, e.g. by moving series-parallel.combined-values to ['core'] for era 2023_2025 or by splitting it into a Core series/parallel combined-resistance detail and a Supplement parallel-calculation detail

gaps.message: Printed part: 3(c)(i). Official code 4.3.2 (Series and parallel circuits). The credit for the three resistance values requires the combined-resistance relations RA = 2R (two resistors in series) and RC = R / 2 (two resistors in parallel) - MS 3(c)(i) "RA = 2.86, RB = 3.04 and RC = 3.11 (ohm)". The owning detail series-parallel.combined-values is stored with applicability ["supplement"] in the pinned overlay, while the printed 2023-2025 syllabus (PDF page 32, printed page 30) shows the combined resistance of two or more resistors in series in the CORE column (Core body x0 ~79.4) and only the parallel treatment in the Supplement column (x0 ~326.0) - the printed column contradicts the pin. This row is a P6 all_candidates (alternative-to-practical) row, so a Supplement content selection is not lawful and the printed statement has no exact same-tier Core owner; the Core sibling series-parallel.rules-and-lamps does not state the combined-resistance relations, so substituting it would not be source-equivalent. Recorded as blocked rather than force-labelled, per the batch-134 reconciliation rule and the same-paper precedent batch-140 0625-2025-w-11-q28, which blocked the combined resistance of 3.0 ohm and 6.0 ohm in parallel on this paper. The remaining marks of the row are carried by the practical-skills labels (practical.data-recording covers 3(c)(i) as recorded data), and the voltmeter and variable-resistor symbols and the R = V / I calculations carry 4.3.1 and 4.2.4, both pinned Core.

gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (Q30 stem and options A-D). The official mark scheme prints answer D - 1 mark for selecting E = IVt as the equation for the electrical energy transferred by a resistor carrying current I at potential difference V for time t. The exact detail for that equation, electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations, is recorded on disk with detail_applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 4.2.5) while the frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/12, so calibration_final._validate_selection rejects the selection. Applicability defect recorded with both exact values: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (SHA256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c, printed page 27, section 4.2.5 Core items 2-3, PDF page 29) "Recall and use the equation for electrical power P = IV" and "Recall and use the equation for electrical energy E = IVt" printed in the Core column (4.2.5 carries no Supplement items). The broad Core sibling electrical-work-power.energy-transfer is expressly not a substitute for the electrical-energy equation (docs/gap-overlay-candidate-v1.md O5: do not substitute electrical-work-power.energy-transfer) and is retained only as a non-mastery placeholder; no label was force-mapped and nothing was promoted.

questions.accessibleText: 36 Which properties must a radioisotope have for its radiation to make it suitable to kill bacteria in food? half-life type of radiation emitted A less than one minute  only B several hours  only C several hours  only D several thousand years  only

gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (printed MCQ Q36 stem and table with the half-life and type-of-radiation-emitted columns, options A-D). The item assesses the printed 2023-2025 Supplement bullet 5.2.4 item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including: ... (b) irradiating food to kill bacteria" (syllabus PDF page 36). The credited row C requires a half-life of several hours and gamma-only emission, i.e. the isotope is selected by its half-life and radiation type for the food-irradiation application. The pinned taxonomy owns only one Supplement detail under mapping 5.2.4, half-life.background-not-subtracted (= Supplement bullet 5.2.4 item 2, calculating half-life from data or decay curves where background radiation has not been subtracted), and no detail at all for the isotope-application bullet 5.2.4 item 3. The printed Core bullets of 5.2.4 are only bullet 1 (define half-life as the time taken for half the nuclei of that isotope in any sample to decay and use it in simple calculations which might involve information in tables or decay curves), recorded as the detail half-life.tables-and-curves, which does not cover choosing a radionuclide for an application; it is the Core owner of subtopic half-life for official code 5.2.4 only, not a source-equivalent label. The nearest candidate labels are not source-equivalent either: nuclear-emissions.fields-and-applications (Supplement, 5.2.2) owns the deflection of the emissions in electric and magnetic fields and the explanation of their relative ionising effects, not isotope selection by half-life and radiation type for an application; nuclear-emissions.nature-ionisation-penetration (Core, 5.2.2) owns the relative ionising and penetrating abilities of alpha, beta and gamma emissions, again not the isotope choice for an application. No Core or Supplement detail in the pinned overlay owns the assessed 5.2.4 item 3(b) food-irradiation isotope-selection operation, so the row stays unresolved rather than forcing a label.
gaps.official_bullet: 5.2.4 item 3 (b) irradiating food to kill bacteria

questions.accessibleText: 33 Some students set up an experiment to measure the count rate for a radioactive source. First, they measure the radioactive background count rate in the laboratory by taking three measurements. Each measurement is taken over a 10-minute period. The table shows their results. number of counts in 10 minutes first measurement second measurement third measurement 170 164 185 Next, the students measure the counts near the radioactive source. This count rate is measured as 949 counts per minute. What is the corrected count rate for the source? A 932 counts per minute B 776 counts per minute C 430 counts per minute D 78 counts per minute

gaps.message: Printed part: question-level (Q33 stem, table and options A-D). The marked operation is the printed 2023-2025 Supplement statement 5.2.1 item 5 'Use measurements of background radiation to determine a corrected count rate' (PDF page 35 / printed page 33, Supplement column x0 = 325.0), credited answer A 932 counts / minute from 949 - (170 + 164 + 185) / 30. The pinned overlay's 5.2.1 mapping owns only the Core-applicable detail radioactivity-detection.background-and-detectors (detail_applicability ['core']), which expresses the Core items 1-4 (background radiation, its sources, detectors/counters and count rate in counts/s or counts/minute) and contains no statement about subtracting background radiation to give a corrected count rate, so no Supplement-band detail is forced and the row stays unresolved. The printed Core item 4 'Use count rate measured in counts / s or counts / minute' is not source-equivalent to the corrected-count-rate operation.

Its owning detail in the pinned overlay is electrical-work-power.power-energy-equations, stored with applicability ["supplement"] (era 2023_2025, official code 4.2.5), while the printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c) prints that bullet in the Core column (PDF page 29 / printed page 27, line x0 = 62.4; the code's printed Supplement column header carries no Supplement items at all, recorded in data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-syllabus-column-evidence.json as printed_core_contradicts_pinned_supplement). Both exact values are therefore: on-disk applicability ["supplement"] versus printed Core column. The frozen packet records paper_tier "core" for 0625/33, so the detail is not selectable. No same-tier Core detail is source-equivalent: electrical-work-power.energy-transfer (core) owns printed Core 4.2.5 item 1 (circuits transfer energy from a source to the circuit components and then into the surroundings) and is carried only as the sibling Core owner under official code 4.2.5, but it does not state P = IV, so the marked part is not legally labelable on a Core paper (settled precedent: batch-133 0625-2025-s-31-q9 (a) and batch-085 0625-2023-w-32-q9 (b) both blocked rather than substituting the Core sibling).

gaps.message: Printed part 9(b)(ii): "The radiation detector is used to measure the thickness of the aluminium sheets and control the gap between the rollers. State the most suitable radioactive source in Table 9.1 for the machine in Fig. 9.2. Explain why this radioactive source is the most suitable and why the other sources are unsuitable." The official mark scheme credits R (B1); "half-life not too short OR half-life is suitable so that source does not need to be replaced often" (B1); "so count rate changes with thickness" (B1); "gamma-rays would not be stopped at all AND alpha-particles would be absorbed by any thickness of aluminium" (B1), i.e. the printed 2023-2025 syllabus 5.2.4 Half-life Supplement item 3 "Explain how the type of radiation emitted and the half-life of an isotope determine which isotope is used for applications including ... (d) measuring and controlling thicknesses of materials with the choice of radiations used linked to penetration and absorption" (PDF page 36 / printed page 34 footer, Supplement column, x0 = 326.0; the Core header prints at x0 = 62.4 and the Supplement header at x0 = 309.0). The pinned taxonomy owns only two details under official code 5.2.4: half-life.tables-and-curves (on-disk detail_applicability ["core"], printed Core item 1 only - the half-life definition and simple calculations from tables or decay curves) and half-life.background-not-subtracted (on-disk detail_applicability ["supplement"], printed Supplement item 2 only - calculating half-life where background radiation has not been subtracted). Neither is source-equivalent to choosing or justifying a radionuclide for a thickness-measuring application: the printed Supplement applications bullet 3(d) has no owning detail, so no detail on any tier carries the assessed statement. This is an owning-detail gap in the pinned taxonomy, not a content gap, and no nearest label was forced. Same settled disposition as batch-114 (0625-2024-w-23-q37), batch-117 (0625-2024-w-42-q10), batch-124 (0625-2025-m-42-q9) and batch-131 (0625-2025-s-22-q35) for the same 5.2.4 item 3 bullet.

questions.accessibleText: 4 A student sets up a flexible track on the laboratory bench. The student investigates the motion of a metal ball as it rolls from rest down the track. The metal ball rolls down the track, up the other side of the track, and comes momentarily to rest at a height h above the bench before rolling back down again. Plan an experiment to investigate how one variable affects the size of this height h. The apparatus available includes: • flexible track • two clamps, bosses and stands to support the track • selection of metal balls. Fig. 4.1 shows how the flexible track is supported. stand h clamp flexible track metal ball path taken by ball Fig. 4.1 You are not required to do the investigation. In your plan: • state the one variable you have chosen to investigate • list any additional apparatus needed • explain how to do the experiment • state the key variables to be kept constant • draw a table, with column headings, to show how to display the readings (you are not required to enter any readings in the table) • explain how to use the readings to reach a conclusion. gaps.message: Printed part 2(e)(i) of 0625-2025-w-53-q2 materially assesses COMBINED RESISTANCE and has no tier-legal owner on this all_candidates P5 paper. The question connects one, two and three IDENTICAL resistance wires in parallel (circuits A, B and C, all at l = 95.0 cm) and asks the candidate to record RA, then calculate RB = R x 2 (from circuit B) and RC = R x 3 (from circuit C) and to compare them (2(e)(ii)); MS 2(e)(i) credits 'calculations correct' and 'RA RB and RC within 10% of each other', i.e. the equal-resistor case of the parallel combined-resistance relation, and 2(e)(ii) reasons on the same values. The printed official 2023-2025 syllabus (sha256 ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c) places the combined-resistance statements in 4.3.2 Series and parallel circuits on syllabus PDF page 30 (printed page 28): Core item 6 (x0 = 62.4 / 79.4) 'State that the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel is less than that of either resistor by itself' and Supplement item 10 (x0 = 309.0) 'Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel'. On disk the era 2023_2025 code 4.3.2 owns exactly two details: series-parallel.rules-and-lamps with detail_applicability ['core'] and series-parallel.combined-values with detail_applicability ['supplement']; only series-parallel.combined-values owns the combined-resistance statements, and it is pinned supplement, so the printed-Core parallel statement has no same-tier owner and the Core sibling series-parallel.rules-and-lamps is not source-equivalent. This is an all_candidates P5 paper, so taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects a Supplement content selection ('all_candidates content selection must use Core or practical skills'); no Core-adjacent detail was substituted and the part is not labelled. Same settled disposition and same operation as batch-138 0625-2025-s-53-q3 (parts were also supplied by the question paper there) and batch-139 0625-2025-s-63-q3, and the same blocked class as batch-140 0625-2025-w-11-q28. The remaining marks of the row are carried by the code-free practical primary, the practical_skills entries and the Core 4.2.4 / 4.2.2 secondaries; the row keeps its practical evidence and is left unresolved for a taxonomy-owner decision.
gaps.official_bullet: 4.3.2 item 6 (Core print) 'State that the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel is less than that of either resistor by itself' / item 10 (Supplement print) 'Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel'
gaps.proposedMaterialConcept: an era-scoped taxonomy re-seal that gives the printed-Core parallel combined-resistance statement a Core-applicability owner on all_candidates practical papers

gaps.message: Printed part 2(d)(i) of 0625-2025-w-63-q2 materially assesses the COMBINED RESISTANCE of identical wires connected in parallel: the student records RA as the value of R from Circuit A (one wire), then calculates RB = R x 2 from the resistance of the two-wire parallel combination in Circuit B and RC = R x 3 from the three-wire parallel combination in Circuit C, i.e. the single-wire resistance is obtained from the parallel-combination resistance. MS 2(d)(i) credits 'RA = 8.06, RB = 7.46 and RC = 7.50 (ohm) OR RA = 8.1, RB = 7.4 OR 7.5 and RC = 7.5 (ohm)'. Official code 4.3.2 (Series and parallel circuits). The owning detail series-parallel.combined-values is stored with applicability ['supplement'] in the pinned overlay, while the printed 2023-2025 syllabus splits the combined-resistance statements across the two columns: 4.3.2 Core item 4 'Calculate the combined resistance of two or more resistors in series' and Core item 6 'State that the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel is less than that of either resistor by itself' are printed in the CORE column (x0 = 62.4 / body x0 = 79.4), and only the parallel calculation Supplement item 10 'Calculate the combined resistance of two resistors in parallel' is printed in the Supplement column (x0 = 309.0 / body x0 = 326.0); the split is recorded verbatim in data/classification/source-problems/taxonomy-syllabus-column-evidence.json (detail_id series-parallel.combined-values, verdict_vs_pinned printed_spans_both_columns, pdf_page 30, printed_page 28, pinned applicability ['supplement']), and the pinned syllabus sha256 is ddacef724f9381658c74b7fe8280a4408c4a513235291ac3f604dbc69dbd5c5c. This row is a P6 all_candidates (alternative-to-practical) paper, so a Supplement content selection is not lawful - taxonomy_tools._selection_error rejects it with 'all_candidates content selection must use Core or practical skills' - and the Core sibling series-parallel.rules-and-lamps does not state the combined-resistance relations, so substituting it would not be source-equivalent. Recorded as blocked rather than force-labelled, per the batch-134 reconciliation rule and the same-series settled precedents 0625-2025-s-63-q3 (blocked at 3(c)(i)) and 0625-2025-s-53-q3 (blocked at (d)(i)). The remaining marks of the row are carried by the code-free practical primary, the practical_skills entries and the Core 4.3.1 / 4.2.4 / 4.2.2 secondaries.
